newsitem.title: UK: Palm oil firm on holiday affected European market.
newsitem.headline: Palm oil firm on holiday affected European market.

text.p: Palm oil prices were firm at the opening of the European vegetable oil market on Wednesday, but business was slow owing to the Queen's Day holiday in the Netherlands.
Data released by cargo surveyors Caleb and SGS boosted futures prices in Kuala Lumpur which in turn supported prices in Europe.
Malaysia's Caleb Brett put Malaysia's March bulk palm oil exports at 631,334 tonnes against its estimate of 620,004 for March, local traders said.
Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) Malaysia Sdn Bhd said it estimated Malaysia's palm oil exports for April at 641,520 tonnes against 608,638 tonnes in March.
Crude palm oil cif Europe opened $2.50 up with no business reported.
Among products RBD palm oil traded at $569 for March while in trading olein fetched $595 for Jun, $585 for Jul and $577.50 and $580 for Jul/Aug.
Lauric oils opened mixed with coconut oil unchanged to $2.50 up and palmkernel oil unchanged to $2.50 down.
The soft oil sector was very thin with offers for soy oil 1.50 to two guilders up and rape oil 1.25 to two guilders higher,
"I don't think any one is even going to try and trade at these levels," said one trader.
